title: Dynamic Prefill Healer and Kernel Fallthrough for Fragmented KV Pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Issue: In long-lived multi-tenant workloads the paged KV cache develops microscopic fragmentation and slot scattering that causes frequent prefill stalls and suboptimal kernel selection. This ticket designs and implements a Dynamic Prefill Healer that opportunistically coalesces nearby fragments and a kernel fallthrough strategy that routes prefill/decode work to compatible kernels on heterogeneous HW when preferred kernels are congested. Goal: reduce prefill tail latency and prefill-induced decode stalls without increasing steady-state token cost by >5%.
technical_design: 1) Fragment fingerprinting: lightweight bloom-based summaries per shard to detect co-located fragments that are safe to coalesce at background priority. 2) Healer waves: periodic low-priority coalescing passes that merge adjacent fragments into contiguous slab regions, with occupancy-aware backoff to avoid thrashing. 3) Kernel fallthrough: maintain a capability matrix for kernels (quantization, sequence-length, sparse-support) and a soft-fallback policy that picks the next-best kernel when the preferred kernel's queue depth or stall metric exceeds a threshold. 4) Admission and prefill pacing: prefill admission controller that stages prefill into micro-waves sized by current decode concurrency, with pre-emptible slots for healers. 5) Telemetry: add prefill-wave histograms, fragment-coalescence counts, and kernel-fallback rates to the runtime metrics to evaluate regressions.
tradeoffs: Background coalescing reduces fragmentation but uses GPU cycles; mitigate via adaptive backoff and pre-emptible scheduling.

Kernel fallthrough increases variability in quality/cost tradeoffs when selecting quantized kernels; restrict fallthrough to kernels with verified functional equivalence and add a quality-safety gate for risky model variants.
Aggressive prefill packing lowers per-token cost but may increase tail latency under contention; use occupancy-aware sizing to balance.
acceptance_criteria: Average prefill tail (95th pct) reduced by >=15% on benchmark workloads (multi-tenant chat traces)
No steady-state token cost regression >5% across representative workload profiles
Kernel-fallback does not increase model output divergence beyond existing thresholds (unit tests + eval set)
Healer background passes can be throttled off without causing correctness issues
